answer: A concrete Sybil defense is differential admission pricing: each new identity pays an entry fee that scales with how many keys the same social neighborhood has already admitted, so a cluster of clones exhausts its own cheap quota quickly. A jetty of coordinated registrations cannot hide because the fee is computed from graph distance, and a sonnet of spoofed neighborhoods fails when attested links are checked. An anchor of well-separated, genuine growth still pays a modest price. The attacker's cost is raising fees for every sibling clone.
